title: Give every thread its own element
starter:
let launch (blocks : int) (size : int) (x : int array) : int array =
  let out = Array.make (Array.length x) 0 in
  for b = 0 to blocks - 1 do
    for t = 0 to size - 1 do
      let i = t in
      out.(i) <- x.(i) * 2
    done
  done;
  out
hints: Look at the line that sets `i`. Block 0 gets the right elements. Which elements does block 1 get?
Block `b` starts where the blocks before it end. Each of them covers `size` elements.
Write `let i = size * b + t in`.

answer.code:
let launch (blocks : int) (size : int) (x : int array) : int array =
  let out = Array.make (Array.length x) 0 in
  for b = 0 to blocks - 1 do
    for t = 0 to size - 1 do
      let i = size * b + t in
      out.(i) <- x.(i) * 2
    done
  done;
  out
answer.explain: A thread is told two numbers, its block and its place in the block. Block b starts at element size * b, so thread t of block b handles element size * b + t. With t alone, every block handles the first size elements again and the rest are never written.
